architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk

decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Run at least two independent repeats and compute the arithmetic mean SI_15_60 across repeats. Accept the combined resin-modification result as supporting H-RESIN over H-CORE if the mean SI_15_60 is below 3.80%, with each repeat also below 3.80%. The 3.80% threshold is half the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction for reactive mass fraction 0.8000.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: The primary observable is a direct isothermal thermal-hold measurement and does not depend on a rheological regularity measured in the same chemistry family. It therefore remains admissible for the resin-modified candidate, but the result must not be used to claim transfer of the unmodified-family temperature-response shape or state-transfer reconstruction.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: Falsify H-RESIN if the arithmetic mean SI_15_60 across at least two independent repeats is at or above 7.61%, the linear-dilution prediction. Falsify H-CORE if the arithmetic mean is below 3.80%. Results from 3.80% through 7.60% do not falsify either hypothesis at the prespecified resolution. This experiment cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL because both predict the same low-drift regime when the minor tackifier axis is active.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: If H-RESIN is falsified by SI_15_60 at or above 7.61%, run a matched-window 120 C hold using an acrylic-only composition at comparable acrylic loading and zero minor tackifier to test the axis-specific prediction. If H-CORE is falsified instead, run that acrylic-only matched hold to distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured at 120 C over the 15-60 minute matched window
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C41 directly interrogates the declared failure mode, uses the supported 15% acrylic-like and 5% minor-tackifier-like region, and separates the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction from the 3.80% superlinear-suppression threshold by more than the declared 2.00 percentage-point resolution. It is a formulation-level rheological test only; it cannot attribute suppression to one modifier axis or establish a molecular mechanism.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator in selecting S1C41::M-HOLD-120, including their tie-break toward the smallest acrylic loading in the stable top set and the direct drift measurement. I accepted the Skeptic's objection that H-RESIN and H-DUAL remain entangled and limited the interpretation accordingly. The binding chemistry audit was followed: modified-chemistry M-ANCHOR cards are inadmissible, while this direct M-HOLD-120 card remains admissible.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local rheological regularities were measured in the original PUR reactive-core formulation family represented by the original E1-E3 formulations, with the E1 +P chemical perturbation treated separately. The intended experiment would stay inside this family only as a candidate using the audited local acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like modifier axes; chemistry-changing additives outside that audited boundary would require direct verification rather than transfer of the local regularities.
planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged 120 C melt residence (thermal-hold drift), with the mechanism of suppression by formulation modifiers unresolved.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original 120 C holds measured SI_15_60 of 9.51% for E1 and 51.54% for E5 over the same 15-60 min window, establishing a large local stability contrast.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only two original formulations have thermal-hold data, with four time points spanning 15-90 min at 120 C; E1 has one reported run and E5 has one reported run. Thus the time-dependent drift coordinate is sparsely sampled and does not resolve modifier-axis behavior, whereas temperature response has seven measured sweep runs across E1-E3 and realized viscosity level has repeated E2 observations, albeit with large spread.
measurement_requirements: Run a matched-window 120 C thermal hold with viscosity recorded at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min, using at least two independent repeats and reporting SI_15_60 directly.
Measure matched compositions along the acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like axes so that acrylic-only behavior can be compared with compositions containing a nonzero minor tackifier fraction.
Compare the observed drift with the pre-specified linear-dilution prediction E1_drift multiplied by reactive mass fraction, using the 2 percentage-point declared discrimination resolution.
Record sufficient preparation and process-history information to distinguish formulation-axis effects from realization or process-state variation.
planner.scientific_question: At matched 120 C residence conditions, does modifier-induced drift follow linear dilution of the reactive core (H-CORE), become substantially more suppressed than linear dilution by resin modification (H-RESIN), and is low drift obtained only when the minor tackifier-like axis is active rather than from the acrylic-like axis alone (H-DUAL)?

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: The candidate is resin-modified and therefore outside the chemistry family in which the local shared thermal-response shape was measured. However, M-HOLD-120 reads thermal-hold drift directly and does not infer it from that shared shape, so the observable remains admissible under the binding audit. The result directly tests the isothermal time-coordinate hypotheses, but transfer of the local rheological shape is not assumed.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If matched 15-60 min drift is below 3.80% across at least two repeats, the result supports H-RESIN over H-CORE by showing suppression below half the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction. Because the minor tackifier axis is active, this outcome does not distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If matched 15-60 min drift is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the result is consistent with H-CORE's linear-dilution prediction. H-DUAL remains unresolved because this experiment contains a nonzero minor tackifier fraction.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A drift between 3.80% and 7.61%, or a result obscured by repeat-to-repeat variation near the 2.00 percentage-point discrimination threshold, would not cleanly adjudicate H-CORE versus H-RESIN. It would also leave H-RESIN versus H-DUAL unresolved; an acrylic-only hold is required for that distinction.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: Deterministically tied, but uses a larger 17.5% acrylic-like loading without improving hypothesis discrimination, interpretability, uncertainty reduction, or decision relevance.
Deterministically tied, but uses a larger 20% acrylic-like loading and therefore imposes a larger formulation departure than necessary for the same direct drift test.
Deterministically tied, but uses a larger 22.5% acrylic-like loading with no additional hypothesis separation.
Deterministically tied, but uses the largest 25% acrylic-like loading in the set and is therefore the least conservative intervention despite identical information value.
It retains the same direct observable and hypothesis coverage but moves the minor-tackifier loading to 7.5%, outside the repeated 4.8-6.4% cluster, introducing extrapolation risk and lowering VOI.

proposer.reasoning: The declared failure mode is thermal-hold drift, and M-HOLD-120 directly measures the least-resolved coordinate with no model-fit or chemistry-shape transfer. S1C41 lies within the externally supported 15-25% acrylic and 3-10% minor-tackifier regions, uses the repeatedly supported 5% tackifier level, and separates the linear-dilution prediction from superlinear suppression at the stated 2.00 percentage-point resolution. It cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL because both predict the same low-drift regime when the tackifier axis is active.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards have identical deterministic VOI component vectors and are genuinely tied. S1C41 is selected because it uses the smallest acrylic-like loading in the tied set while retaining the independently supported 5% minor-tackifier region, minimizing modifier burden and preserving full two-axis coverage. Its reactive mass fraction is 0.8000, giving a clear linear-dilution comparator of 7.61% and a superlinear-suppression threshold of 3.80%.

residual_decision_risk: H-RESIN versus H-DUAL remains unresolved because both axes are active.
The protocol lacks a predefined repeat-aggregation rule and stronger process-state control; near-threshold results may remain difficult to adjudicate.
The binding chemistry audit permits the direct thermal-hold observable but does not support transferring the unmodified chemistry shared thermal-response shape to this resin-modified formulation.
The result must not be generalized to temperature-response transfer, state-transfer reconstruction, or a molecular reaction mechanism without direct supporting measurements.
The deterministic ranking is tied and stable, but stability is not evidence that the selected experiment or its hypotheses are scientifically correct.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The objection is valid: S1C41 changes both modifier axes, so a direct low-drift result can test the combined intervention against the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction but cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL or attribute suppression to either axis. This limitation does not invalidate the proposed direct M-HOLD-120 experiment or require replacing it with an experiment explicitly identified in the payload. It constrains the interpretation and supports a later acrylic-only matched hold as a follow-up. The tie among the five top cards does not resolve this entanglement because all tied cards use the same dual-axis intervention and measurement plan.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The tied top set is unchanged across all 25 re-weightings, with top_experiment_set_stability of 1.0, intervention-family stability of 1.0, and measurement-plan stability of 1.0. No recommendation_flip_boundary is reached for any weight term over the 0.5 to 1.5 sweep, so no tested weighting changes the decision. The base margin to the first strictly lower experiment is 0.004583. These results support decision stability of the transparent VOI ranking, not confidence in the experiment or its scientific outcome.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The primary SI_15_60 observable stays within direct measurement support because M-HOLD-120 records viscosity at 120 C during the matched 15-60 minute window and does not reuse the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI shared thermal-response shape. The composition itself is outside the validated shared-shape chemistry family, so any temperature-response or state-transfer claim would require a direct M-SWEEP verification in the resin-modified chemistry.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The protocol directly measures the quantity needed for the criterion, and the H-CORE versus H-RESIN predictions, 7.608% versus 3.804%, differ by 3.804 percentage points, exceeding the declared 2.00 percentage-point resolution. However, the protocol does not specify an aggregation rule or stronger state-control procedure for the minimum two repeats; process_state_risk is 0.75 and measurement_catalog.controls_process_state is false. The criterion is therefore attainable, but borderline results may not be robustly adjudicated.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Any claim that the acrylic-like axis causes suppression, or that the minor tackifier is specifically responsible for suppression, would be unsupported. Only a combined-resin effect versus linear dilution could be claimed.
objections.objection: S1C41 changes both modifier axes simultaneously: AC1920 is 15.0% and TK100 is 5.0%, while the reactive mass fraction is reduced to 0.8000. A low SI_15_60 therefore cannot be attributed to acrylic modification, tackifier modification, or their interaction. It can only test the combined intervention against the 7.61% linear-dilution comparator. The proposed experiment consequently cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL, as the Proposer correctly admits.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment cannot support selection between the broad resin-modification hypothesis and the tackifier-required specialization hypothesis, despite the ranked card's scientific_hypotheses_addressed listing all three.
objections.objection: The declared hypothesis coverage is incomplete: proposer.hypotheses_not_separated explicitly lists H-DUAL. At S1C41, H-RESIN and H-DUAL both predict 3.804% drift, while H-CORE predicts 7.608%; the 3.804 percentage-point separation from H-CORE exceeds the declared 2.00 percentage-point resolution, but the H-RESIN/H-DUAL separation is zero and therefore below resolution.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result near 3.80% or 7.61% could be classified inconsistently, weakening the claimed falsification of H-CORE or H-RESIN and making an intermediate result more likely to be attributed to formulation rather than preparation-state variation.
objections.objection: The SI_15_60 observable is directly measurable under M-HOLD-120, so the thresholds are physically attainable, but the protocol specifies only 'at least two independent repeats' and does not define how repeat results are aggregated for the criteria 'below 3.80% across at least two repeats' and 'at or above 7.61%'. With measurement process-state control marked false, missing_process_fields equal to 6, and process_state_risk scored 0.75, repeat-to-repeat state variation could make the boundary outcome non-adjudicable even though the nominal 3.804-point hypothesis separation exceeds the 2.00-point resolution.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The direct hot-hold result could be overgeneralized into an unsupported claim that the unmodified chemistry's thermal-response regularity transfers to the resin-modified formulation.
objections.objection: S1C41 is in chemistry family resin_modified:ac1920+tk100, which the audit marks modified_chemistry_unvalidated with shared_shape_use equal to verification_only. The proposal correctly avoids M-ANCHOR and does not use the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI shared thermal-response shape to obtain SI_15_60. Thus the primary observable is direct and does not leave the measured rheological shape domain. However, any interpretation extending the result to temperature-response transfer, shared-shape behavior, or 120-130 C reconstruction would be outside the measured chemistry support without an M-SWEEP direct verification.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result would still be a valid direct observation of matched-window drift, but it would be misused as evidence for a single modifier mechanism.
objections.objection: The primary observable SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 is read directly from the 15 and 60 minute measurements in M-HOLD-120; it requires no model fit, extrapolation, or imputation. This part of the proposal survives the attack. The weakness is not the observable itself but the attribution of its change under the two-axis composition.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment could be reported as having established a molecular reaction or encounter-frequency mechanism, although M-HOLD-120 measures only isothermal viscosity drift.
objections.objection: No unmeasured target outcome or validation-formulation identity is used in the stated rationale; the acceptance and falsification rules are prospective and pre-specified. The registered H-RESIN wording invokes effective concentration and encounter frequency, but the experiment can adjudicate only the formulation-level drift prediction, not that molecular explanation. The payload's claim_boundary correctly limits the hypotheses to formulation-level rheological mechanisms.

skeptic.recommended_change: Add a matched-window 120 C hold for an acrylic-only composition at a comparable acrylic loading with zero minor tackifier, and analyze it under the same SI_15_60 protocol. Also predefine the repeat aggregation rule and standardize the six missing preparation/process-history fields before interpreting near-threshold results.
skeptic.strongest_objection: S1C41 moves the acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like axes together, so its direct SI_15_60 result cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL or assign suppression to either modifier axis. It can only compare the combined intervention with the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_GJJ_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 GJJ day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is BINDING. The cards it marks inadmissible were removed before ranking and are not selectable. You may state that you disagree with the rule and why; naming a removed card is an invalid output.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.
